lines.text: Meet Gluco. It turns wearable data into a simple daily score, for people at risk of diabetes, and for their care team.
A clinician sees the whole panel: pinned widgets, cohort trends, and every patient, ranked by who needs attention.
Sensor data streams in live. Here we replay last night, one hour every second.
Patient thirteen's score is collapsing. And once the replay reaches the present, their heart rate, movement and skin temperature stream in every second.
So the doctor asks Gluco why, and for a heatmap.
The agent explains the drop from the data, then builds a widget: it designs the chart, fetches the data, runs a privacy compliance check, and binds it to a live query.
One click pins it to the dashboard.
Suggested prompts make it faster still. The five lowest scores, ranked and pinned.
Back on the panel, both new widgets are pinned, and they stay live as new data arrives.
Now, the same story from the patient's side.
Patients get plain language: their score, their week, and their own live vitals. They only ever see their own data.
They can build widgets too. A heart rate tile, pinned in seconds.
And when a question needs a doctor, Gluco says so, instead of guessing.
